2.note: Here, **hand** and **hands** represent the control or direction of a person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly, here and in verses 3 and 6. Alternate translation: [under the direction of Asaph … under the supervision of the king]

3.note: The name “Shimei” appears after Jeshaiah in one Hebrew manuscript and in the ancient Greek translation. That makes sense, since Shimei is listed in v. 17 among the clan leaders who received assignments. It appears that his name has been accidentally omitted from the standard Hebrew text as we have it today. You may want to follow the alternative reading of the ancient Greek translation, or you may want to follow the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [Gedaliah and Zeri and Jeshaiah and Shimei, Hashabiah and Mattithiah]

5.note: The author is using the term **words** to mean a promise that God spoke to Heman by using words. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in fulfillment of the promise of God]

The author is speaking as if Heman were an animal with a **horn** that God could **lift up**. An animal that lifts its horn is demonstrating strength and assertiveness. Accordingly, in this culture, a horn represented strength and dignity. If it would be clearer in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to make him strong] or [to give him dignity]
Here the word **For** introduces not a reason but an elaboration. Alternate translation: [Indeed,]

6.note: The author is speaking of the temple that the Israelites would build for Yahweh as if it were a **house** in which Yahweh would live. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the temple of Yahweh … the temple of God]

7.note: The author is using the term **brothers** to mean “relatives.” Alternate translation: [their kinsmen] or [their fellow Levites]

The expression **having been taught** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [who had learned]

8.note: The author is referring to all of the Levites he has listed by naming two extremes, **small** and **great**, and by describing two main positions that these musicians could be in, that of a **teacher** or that of a **student**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [no matter how important a man was and no matter how accomplished a musician he was]

9.note: If your language would not represent a number in a form such as **first** or **second**, you could represent such numbers in a form that your language would use, here and through verse 31. Alternate translation: [lot number one … lot number two]

The author is using the adjective **second** as a noun to mean a certain kind of thing, a lot. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate such adjectives with equivalent phrases, here and through verse 31. Alternate translation: [the second lot]

If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information that this first lot selected **Joseph** before the information that Joseph belonged to the family of **Asaph**. Alternate translation: [for Joseph son of Asaph]

The author must mean implicitly that 12 of Joseph’s brothers (relatives) and sons served with him. Otherwise, the list does not total 288, as verse 7 states. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [for Joseph, his sons and his brothers, 12]

The author makes clear in this instance that the expression “his sons and his brothers” in the rest of the chapter includes the named individual, so you do not need to indicate that in the following verses.

Since Gedaliah’s literal brothers are listed separately, it is clear that here the author is using the term **brothers** to mean other relatives who served with him. Alternate translation: [and his kinsmen]

11.note: The name **Izri** is a variant of the name “Zeri” in verse 3. Recall whether your translation team decided to use the same name for a given person in each instance where he appears or whether you decided to use the name that the biblical author does, even if that is a variant. Alternate translation: [for Zeri]

14.note: The name **Jesharelah** is a variant of the name “Asharelah” in verse 2. You may have decided to use the same name for a given person in each instance where he appears. Alternate translation: [Asharelah]

18.note: The name **Azarel** is a variant of the name “Uzziel” in verse r. You may have decided to use the same name for a given person in each instance where he appears. Alternate translation: [Uzziel]
